scope: Defensive source-study catalog for the trimmed local HEVD source copy. No build, no driver load, no device request, no exploit code and no payload.
taxonomy: method=Source Review marks study entries. Presence is not evaluated because these are source subjects, not host binaries. Gap is NOT EVALUATED by design.

techniques.name: Device Control Boundary
techniques.abuse: Not an offensive technique. This entry marks the device-control path as a source-review subject: entry points, access scope, and buffer validation before use.
techniques.probe: Inventory only. No device request is sent and no driver is loaded.
telemetry: Driver load auditing on a real lab host
Code integrity telemetry on a real lab host
techniques.detection: Review the dispatch routine for explicit input and output length checks, fixed buffer methods, and access restrictions. On a managed host, rely on driver-load and code-integrity events, not exploit traces.
hardening: Validate InputBufferLength and OutputBufferLength before any read or write.
Prefer a fixed buffer method with an explicit minimum and maximum size.
Scope device access to the accounts that actually need it.

tree.a: Locate the driver entry and the dispatch table assignment
Record where device control requests are handled
Check length and access validation before buffer use

fix: Document the dispatch function and each validation step in RESEARCH.
Add a Code Audit rule that flags device-control handlers without nearby length checks.
Treat any review gap as a study note, never as proof of exploitability.

techniques.name: Fixed-Size Copy Review
techniques.abuse: Not an offensive technique. This entry studies copy operations where destination capacity and source length must be checked.
techniques.probe: Inventory only. No buffer is allocated or written by NetTruder.
techniques.detection: Look for unbounded copy APIs, length values taken from callers, and fixed-size local buffers. Confirm that every copied length is bounded by the destination size.
hardening: Use bounded copy helpers with an explicit destination size.
Check arithmetic before allocation or copy.
Prefer safe string functions and length-preserving conversions.

tree.a: Find a copy call in a vulnerable-study source file
Trace the destination size and source length
Write a defensive finding with the correct bounded API

fix: Replace unbounded copies with size-checked equivalents.
Add regression tests that use oversized input in a controlled unit test, not a live driver.
Link each Code Audit hit to this RESEARCH entry.

techniques.name: Pool Lifetime and Size Review
techniques.abuse: Not an offensive technique. This entry studies allocation size, initialization, and free paths in kernel pool code.
techniques.probe: Inventory only. No pool is allocated or freed by NetTruder.
telemetry: Driver Verifier on a separate lab host
Pool monitoring telemetry on a separate lab host
techniques.detection: Review allocation size arithmetic, tag use, initialization, and every free path. Look for double-free or use-after-free conditions by reading ownership changes, not by triggering them.
hardening: Check multiplication and addition before allocation.
Initialise allocated structures before use.
Clear pointers after free and enforce single ownership.

tree.a: Find the allocation call and its size expression
Follow initialisation and ownership through the function
Record the safe free path and any gap

fix: Use checked integer arithmetic for allocation sizes.
Document single-owner lifetime rules in the RESEARCH note.
Enable Driver Verifier only in a separate disposable lab, never on a production host.

techniques.name: Object Lifetime Review
techniques.abuse: Not an offensive technique. This entry studies how an object can be referenced after its lifetime has ended.
techniques.probe: Inventory only. No object is created or released by NetTruder.
telemetry: Pool and handle telemetry on a separate lab host
techniques.detection: Trace allocation, reference, free, and nulling. A defensive finding is any path that can still reach an object after the free branch.
hardening: Use reference-counted ownership for shared objects.
Set pointers to null immediately after free.
Avoid storing raw pointers in longer-lived structures.

tree.a: Mark allocation and free branches in the source
Trace every later dereference of the same pointer
Write the safe ownership rule in RESEARCH

fix: Document the ownership rule next to the struct definition.
Prefer APIs that return owned handles rather than raw pointers.
Do not attempt dynamic validation on a production host.

techniques.name: Integer Arithmetic Review
techniques.abuse: Not an offensive technique. This entry studies arithmetic that decides buffer size or copy length. A wrapped value can make a bound check pass while the real size is too large; study the pattern, never a trigger.
techniques.probe: Inventory only. No arithmetic is executed by NetTruder.
techniques.detection: Look for multiplication, addition, or subtraction on sizes that come from callers, especially arithmetic inside a comparison. A fixed-width value can wrap, so the check reads a small number while the real requirement is large. Confirm checked arithmetic and a final bound against the destination capacity.
hardening: Use checked integer helpers before allocation.
Reject sizes above a documented maximum.
Verify the bound after the arithmetic, not before it.
Use size_t consistently for lengths.

tree.a: Locate arithmetic that feeds a size or length
Identify the type and maximum possible value
Record the checked-arithmetic fix

fix: Replace raw arithmetic with checked helpers.
Add a maximum-size constant and reject larger requests.
Verify the bound after the calculation so a wrapped value cannot pass it.
Attach the rule hit to this RESEARCH entry.

techniques.name: Initialisation Review
techniques.abuse: Not an offensive technique. This entry studies structures that are read before every field is assigned.
techniques.probe: Inventory only. No stack memory is read or written by NetTruder.
techniques.detection: Find local structures or buffers that are copied or returned. Confirm that all fields are assigned or explicitly zeroed before use.
hardening: Use designated initialisation where possible.
Zero structures before populating them.
Enable compiler warnings for uninitialised variables.

tree.a: Find a local structure used as output
Check every field for an assignment
Record the safe initialisation pattern

fix: Initialise the whole structure before field assignment.
Treat compiler warnings as build failures in the study notes.
Do not attempt to read uninitialised memory at runtime.

techniques.name: User Pointer Boundary Review
techniques.abuse: Not an offensive technique. This entry studies buffers that cross the user-to-kernel boundary and must be validated once and copied safely.
techniques.probe: Inventory only. No user buffer is probed or read by NetTruder.
telemetry: Kernel-mode code integrity telemetry on a separate lab host
techniques.detection: Review whether user pointers are probed, captured once into kernel memory, and validated inside exception handling. Flag repeated reads of the same user buffer without a consistent snapshot.
hardening: Probe user buffers before access.
Copy user data into a kernel-owned buffer once, then validate the copy.
Use exception handling around every user-buffer access.

tree.a: Locate a buffer that comes from a caller
Check probe, copy, and validation order
Record a single-snapshot defensive pattern

fix: Probe and copy once, then use only the kernel-owned copy.
Keep validation next to the copy, not next to later reads.
Never send a device request from NetTruder.

techniques.name: Kernel Mitigation Mapping
techniques.abuse: Not an offensive technique. This entry maps bug classes to defensive controls and platform mitigations without testing bypasses.
techniques.probe: Inventory only. No mitigation is enabled, disabled, or bypassed.
telemetry: Driver Verifier in a disposable lab only
techniques.detection: Use host policy state and driver-load events to judge exposure. A source finding is not proof that a mitigation can be defeated.
hardening: Keep VBS, HVCI and code integrity enabled where supported.
Inventory third-party drivers and remove abandoned ones.
Use Driver Verifier only in a controlled test VM.

tree.a: Select a bug class from the catalog
Map it to the control that reduces exposure
Record what the control does and does not prove

fix: Write one RESEARCH note per bug class with control state and evidence limits.
Never turn a security control off to make a study result more interesting.
Treat an Application Control block as a positive defensive result.
